::: {#rem-channel-coding-meaning}
#### Reliable communication at a positive rate

@exm-repetition-code buys a lower error rate with a lower rate,
and repetition alone drives the error to $0$ only as the rate falls to $0$.
@thm-channel-coding says that this trade-off is not forced:
over the channel of @exm-bsc-capacity,
long enough codes send about $0.53$ bits per channel use
with an error probability as small as we like.
Above capacity, no code can.

@shannon1948mathematical stated the theorem and sketched its proof.
@cover2006elements [section 7.7] prove part 1 by choosing codewords at random,
and @cover2006elements [section 7.9] prove part 2 with Fano's inequality.
@mackay2003information [chapters 9 and 10] gives another account.

:::
